title: Building Agents Is Trivial Now, Context Is the Next Frontier — Jeff Ng, Unblocked
talk_summary: The speaker argues agent deployment is now easy, but autonomous agents fail because they lack organizational context that humans supply in local loops; his example recommends a harmful change because it missed a Slack discussion and postmortem. He proposes a context engine that connects docs/code/tickets/conversations, reconciles and permission-scopes them, and returns synthesized understanding rather than raw MCP results.

takeaways.what_they_do: Connect code, tickets, docs, and conversations, then reconcile, rank, and scope the data into a synthesized understanding for the agent instead of raw documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Scattered context comes in, grounded context comes out.

takeaways.what_they_do: The failure example came from missing the Slack discussion and postmortem that explained why a setting had been disabled after an outage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It was missing the context from the Slack discussion that happened after the issue

takeaways.technique: Pre-process MCP/tool output into reconciled context
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP gives access to raw results, but the agent is left to decide what to believe, handle conflicts, and avoid flooding its context window.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP is great at access, but access isn't understanding.

takeaways.what_they_do: Background agents can silently misinform when they lack the human context layer that catches missing facts and steers locally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is going to make that mistake silently in the background

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist message history, tool calls, and loop position so long-lived agent runs can resume after crashes without repeating tokens or side effects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Crashing without durability can actually lead to a lot of state loss.

takeaways.technique: Isolated build sandboxes with secret/network limits
takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent-generated and third-party code in isolated sandboxes to prevent secret reads, unnecessary network access, and shared-host damage.
